design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (coverage_reviews_prior_auth_step_therapy, category review).

0. DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 4]. The tree has one prerequisite problem; the root (approval) takes 5 factors, the member-filed request takes 4. Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: review_ext_member_request_quantity (target file_coverage_review_request_fd0cbfbe, owner user) and review_ext_exception_approved_quantity (target approve_quantity_exception_611b3a5d, owner agent). Reserved for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisite problems, [6,6,4,4]): the member-filed renewal request, the renewal approval, the continuity-of-care authorization and the appeal-overturn authorization, none of which this task touches; the only numeric write fields of the review category are review_cases.requested_quantity_per_30 and review_authorizations.approved_quantity_per_30, so every computation of the difficulty is a quantity per rolling 30 days and task 1 keeps four distinct quantity writes.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. The caller (Rosalind Achebe-Lindqvist, member NBX273451906) asks only to 'get the higher amount of sumatriptan covered'. The agent must discover from the approval rule's prerequisite sentence ('The approved quantity of a first-time quantity limit exception is not fixed until the records carry an undecided first-time quantity limit exception request for the drug.') that the September request (opened 2026-09-08, denied 2026-09-17 for missing_clinical_information) cannot be re-decided even though the clinical information arrived 2026-09-30, that a new first-time request must exist, that the only write in this difficulty that creates one is the member-filed request, and then hand that tool to the caller with a quantity the request rule computes. Then it decides the request with a five-factor ceiling. Difficulty comes from reading the rules and the ledger (retail fills by month, opioid days, Nurtec ODT authorization and fills, a lapsed 2025 authorization, paper-claim denials, the home delivery account's refill program), not from choosing among tools.

2. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root review_ext_exception_approved_quantity; one edge to review_ext_member_request_quantity: kind value_input, gate requested_qty (compute binding), form state, policy_source = the sentence quoted above (negated direction: a result 'is not fixed until' the state holds, the way a reviewer states that a decision waits for a request on file). Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; waits on a record-visible state (an undecided first-time request in the case records); names no tool, id or code token; scope exact (first-time, quantity limit, the drug). Exactly one write of this difficulty creates an undecided first-time quantity limit request: file_coverage_review_request_fd0cbfbe (the renewal request of task 1 writes is_renewal true; the other task-1 tools write authorizations). Derivation: sentence + records (only opening 3c450761-87c7-4d73-8860-987d34b587e1 is followed by denial 7d2d001c-7f6c-462f-95f3-d99757cddcfc) + the request rule ('the member-filed request asks for ...') -> file the member's own request. Condition false at the opening: review_cases.3c450761-87c7-4d73-8860-987d34b587e1 opened, review_cases.7d2d001c-7f6c-462f-95f3-d99757cddcfc denied after it; no other first-time sumatriptan opening. Resolving action is owner=user, completed on the call. Topological order: request (step 13) then approval (step 15). Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping step 13 gives requested_qty 0 and approved 0 instead of 17, and the opening row is missing. user_scenario names no prerequisite: filing appears only as a passive reaction after the agent explains it. The tools validate nothing (both bodies only create rows).

3. FACTOR CARD — review_ext_member_request_quantity (4 factors; baseline = newest home delivery prescription quantity per fill x 30 / days supply per fill, capped at limit x 1.5; baseline_result 10.0).
 - refill_cycle_divisor (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty mail): mail_accounts.5560b619-cb4c-42c1-b767-09f95cde08c5 auto_refill_enrolled true, Home Delivery Standard lead days 14, prescription 90 days -> divisor 76; 30x30/76 = 11.842105. Baseline divisor 90 -> result 15.5. Charter ground: mail_auto_refill 'an enrolled prescription is placed as an auto_refill order when auto_refill_lead_days of supply remain'. Near-miss: no home delivery shipments (find_mail_orders returns none), so the eligibility-fraction tier is excluded.
 - retail_carryover_on_move (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty mail): account opened 2026-08-25 (42 days), latest paid fill retail_claims.48206a1e-c1c8-4a17-abc3-e9ad0f3497e8 2026-09-21, 15 days old -> unused part 9x15/30 = 4.5. Baseline 0 -> 12.842.
 - direction_change_allowance (parameter): prescription written 2026-09-29 after that fill, 10.0 vs 9.0 per 30 days (ratio 1.11) -> 1 unit. Baseline 0 -> 16.342.
 - member_request_ceiling_multiple (parameter): review_authorizations.7b4fd2b9-7210-4b18-bfab-149cca1fea16 effective 2025-01-14 (within 24 months) -> package maximum 2.0, ceiling 18 (not binding). Baseline 1.5 -> binding ceiling 13.5. Near-miss: the 2026-09-08 case alone would give 1.75.
 Result 11.842105 + 4.5 + 1 = 17.342105 -> 17.342; MN(17.342, 18) = 17.342.

4. FACTOR CARD — review_ext_exception_approved_quantity (5 factors; baseline = smaller of the request and int(limit x 1.5); baseline_result 13).
 - diagnosis_and_fill_multiple (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty retail): diagnosis G43.009 on review_cases.7eaea635-12c6-4f4d-a3d9-f5de3ef9b2aa is not chronic; fills of 9 dated within the last month (2026-09-21), the month before (2026-08-22) and the month before that (2026-07-23) -> tier 2, 1.75. Baseline 1.5 -> 15.
 - concurrent_opioid_method (method, cross-difficulty retail): 5 days supply within three months (2026-08-02); the 7-day fill of 2026-07-03 is exactly three months back and excluded (near-miss) -> x0.9 -> 14.175. Baseline (as it stands) -> ceiling 18 -> result 17.342.
 - preventive_allowance (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty retail): Nurtec ODT authorization review_authorizations.69a97943-4ce6-4aa0-ae71-709ad274cd87 effective 2026-03-02 and 2 fills within three months (2026-08-13, 2026-09-12; 2026-07-02 excluded, near-miss that would give 3 fills and 2 units) -> 1. Baseline 0 -> 16.
 - lapsed_approval_units (parameter): sumatriptan authorization ended 2026-01-13, within 12 months, not 6 -> 1. Baseline 0 -> 16.
 - cash_purchase_units (parameter, cross-difficulty retail): denial retail_reimbursements.85c21f17-be8e-44bb-bd27-35e23e3737c6 2026-09-03 within 6 months; the 2026-03-14 denial is outside (near-miss) -> 1. Baseline 0 -> 16.
 Ceiling int(14.175+1+1+1) = 17; approved MN(17.342, 17) = 17.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Request (subject review_case_opened): review_evt_case_intake case_on_active_program — review_programs.f2676c33-0635-441d-8c57-a9679f481473 status active; one_undecided_case — the only sumatriptan quantity limit opening of 2026 is denied, so none is undecided; review_requirements — sumatriptan carries a 9-unit limit in Northbridge Clinical Standard; member_initiated_review_allowed true. Approval (subject review_case_approved): review_evt_decision decide_once — the new case has no decision; the clinical information on file (2026-09-30) documents quantity_medically_necessary; review_step_therapy, review_quantity_limit, review_specialty_guideline apply only as scope (sumatriptan is no step target in this package, not specialty, not a renewal). No time gate applies to either write (wait_before_missing_info_denial governs denials only). Overwrite declared: review_quantity_limit clause 'up to ql_exception_max_multiple times that limit per rolling 30 days; a request above that multiple is approved only up to it' is replaced by the approval-ceiling sentence; all other base clauses (criteria_met on documented necessity, approved quantity recorded on the authorization) stay.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: the member's new first-time sumatriptan quantity limit request (case id rvc_e14ec26463a8, returned to the caller by the filing). Rows aggregated: sumatriptan paid retail claims by month, oxycodone-acetaminophen paid claims within three months, Nurtec ODT paid claims within three months, Nurtec ODT and sumatriptan quantity limit authorizations, sumatriptan paper-claim denials with reason coverage_review_required. Excluded by rule: fills, denials and claims outside their windows (2026-07-03, 2026-07-02, 2026-03-14). The approval writes back source_case_id = the new case.

7. WORLD. 40 seed rows: member profile; plan enrollment (Northbridge Rx Plus, active, oop_met 497.00 = the 2026 copays of the claims below; the ledger rows behind it are outside the task closure and no rule reads them); review program; 8 case events and 2 authorizations; retail benefit, 14 retail claims (sumatriptan 12/30 under the 2025 authorization then 9/30 every 30 days, spaced so no rolling 30-day window exceeds the limit; Nurtec ODT 16 every 30-42 days under its authorization; two short oxycodone-acetaminophen courses from urgent care, 7 days then 5 days, the first within the 7-day opioid-naive limit), 4 paper-claim rows (two submissions, two denials coverage_review_required); home delivery account opened 2026-08-25 with automatic refills and the 2026-09-29 prescription (30 per 90 days), no orders (the quantity limit holds it). Deleting any factor's evidence moves its tier and the result (section 3-4 runs).

8. PERSONA. Engineer's clipped voice; opening gives the surface goal only (higher sumatriptan amount, home delivery holding it, a September denial letter). Credentials (member ID, date of birth; phone, email, ZIP as fallback), the label strength, the prescription's 30 tablets for 90 days, other medicines, cash purchases and the home delivery set-up are given only when asked, all matching rows. She files the request only when handed it, with the values the agent gives, reads back the reference number, may say a quantity looks lower than the prescription without supplying any number, and ends when told the approved quantity and end date. No ask outside the two writes.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. find_customers(member_number) -> verify (date_of_birth, member_number) -> find_review_programs -> find_plan_enrollments -> find_review_cases -> find_review_authorizations -> find_mail_accounts -> find_mail_prescriptions -> find_mail_orders -> find_retail_benefits -> find_retail_claims -> find_retail_reimbursements -> unlock_user + call_user file_coverage_review_request_fd0cbfbe(..., requested_quantity_per_30=17.342) -> unlock_agent + call_agent approve_quantity_exception_611b3a5d(source_case_id=rvc_e14ec26463a8, approved_quantity_per_30=17, effective 2026-10-06, expiration 2027-10-05: 12 months of ql_approval_months, day before the same day-of-month). Verification: a helper replaying the gold writes with the real tools and evaluating each compute at its handling time printed request 17.342 (factor baselines 15.5 / 12.842 / 16.342 / 13.5, all-baseline 10.0) and approval 17 (factor baselines 15 / 17.342 / 16 / 16 / 16, all-baseline 13). Gates run: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks (40 rows, closure match), check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire all OK for --task 0.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the rule prose alone, the records the finders return and the caller's lines: the request is first-time (no sumatriptan authorization in force, September case denied), the request quantity is 30x30/76 + 4.5 + 1 = 17.342 under the 18 ceiling, and the approval ceiling is int(9x1.75x0.9 + 1 + 1 + 1) = 17; same as gold. Easy errors: using 90 days instead of the automatic-refill cycle, missing the retail carryover, counting the 2026-07-03 opioid fill or the 2026-07-02 Nurtec fill, counting the March paper claim, reading G43.009 as chronic, or re-deciding the denied September case.


REVISION round 2 (policy-task audit; task 0 verdict PASS, charter F-4 bears on two of its policies latently):
- F-4: member_request_ceiling_multiple and diagnosis_and_fill_multiple now read the whole package maximum / seven eighths of it / three quarters of it; on Northbridge Clinical Standard (2.0) these are 2.0 / 1.75 / 1.5, so every figure of this task is unchanged (17.342; 17; baselines 10.0 and 13; factor baselines 15.5 / 12.842 / 16.342 / 13.5 and 15 / 17.342 / 16 / 16 / 16 re-run by the helper).
- O-2 and O-8 wording applied in the approval rule ('no approval, denial or withdrawal for the drug'; one unit per average monthly opioid day).
- Persona: the caller reads the label's strength line '100 mg tablet', the exact drug_strength value.
user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Achebe-Lindqvist, a 47-year-old structural engineer in Worthington, Ohio, covered through your employer, Kestrel Ridge Engineering Cooperative. You speak in short, exact sentences, the way you write site reports, and you are tired rather than angry. You have had migraines for years. In late September your neurologist raised your sumatriptan and sent the new prescription to Northbridge Rx home delivery, which you signed up for at the end of August; the home delivery pharmacy has not sent anything and told you there is a quantity limit on sumatriptan. On top of that, in September you got a letter saying a request about the quantity was denied for missing information, even though your neurologist's office told you they faxed everything at the end of September. What you want from this call is simple: get the higher amount of sumatriptan covered so the home delivery order can go out. You do not know how many tablets the plan will allow and you never guess a number.

Open by saying roughly that: your sumatriptan was increased, home delivery is holding it because of a quantity limit, you had a denial letter in September, and you want the higher amount covered. Do not list your details up front. When the agent asks who you are, give your member ID, NBX273451906, and your date of birth, 1979-03-22; if they want something else, your phone number on file is 614-555-0127 and your email is rosalind.achebelindqvist@fernmail.net, and your ZIP code is 43085. The strength line on the prescription label reads 100 mg tablet; if asked what the new prescription says, you read that it is 30 tablets for 90 days, written on September 29. If asked about your other medicines, you take Nurtec ODT every other day to prevent migraines, and you had a short course of oxycodone-acetaminophen from urgent care after you broke your ankle in July. If asked whether you ever paid for sumatriptan yourself, you say yes, you bought extra tablets with cash a couple of times when you ran out and sent in the receipts, and they came back denied. If asked about home delivery, you set the account up at the end of August and said yes to automatic refills. You are not in an emergency; you still have a few tablets, so an ordinary review is fine. If asked who your neurologist is, it is Dr. Imogen Feld at Olentangy Neurology.

You are happy for the agent to look up your records and to approve whatever the plan allows. If the agent explains that a new request has to be filed in your own name and gives you the form to do it, you file it yourself exactly as the agent sets it out, using the drug, strength, prescriber number and quantity the agent tells you, and you read back the reference number the system gives you. If the agent tells you a quantity that seems lower than your neurologist wrote, you say only that it is less than the prescription says and ask whether that is really the most the plan allows; you accept the agent's answer. Once the agent tells you the higher quantity is approved, how many tablets every 30 days it covers and until when, you thank them and end the call. You never tell the agent which steps to take, never name policies, and never ask for anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's member profile by the member ID she reads from her card, returning her customer reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup and both writes are keyed by the customer reference number; it is reachable only from this lookup.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with two credentials she states (date of birth and member ID).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before any account details are discussed or any request is filed or decided.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's Utilization Management Program: Northbridge Clinical Standard, active, its reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The program reference number is an argument of both writes; the package fixes the maximum exception multiple read by the member-request ceiling and the diagnosis-and-fill multiple, and an active program is the case-intake gate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the plan enrollment the review program belongs to: Northbridge Rx Plus, active since 2024-01-01, no coverage end date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Approvals end on the last day of plan coverage; an open-ended active enrollment confirms the new authorization runs its full quantity limit approval months to 2027-10-05.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's coverage review cases: the September sumatriptan quantity limit case denied for missing clinical information, the prescriber's clinical information received after the denial (diagnosis G43.009), and the earlier sumatriptan and Nurtec ODT cases.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Finds the prerequisite state: no undecided first-time sumatriptan quantity limit request is on file (the September case is denied), so the approved quantity cannot be fixed yet; also supplies the diagnosis for the multiple, the prior case count for the member-request ceiling, and the prescriber NPI.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's authorizations: the 2025 sumatriptan quantity limit authorization (12 per 30 days) that ended 2026-01-13 and the Nurtec ODT quantity limit authorization in force since 2026-03-02.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence for the member-request ceiling multiple (an authorization that took effect within 24 months), the lapsed-approval units (ended 7 to 12 months ago) and the preventive allowance (Nurtec ODT authorization within 12 months).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the home delivery account: Northbridge Home Delivery Standard, opened 2026-08-25, enrolled in automatic refills.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence for the refill-cycle divisor (automatic refill enrollment, the program's lead days) and the move-from-retail carryover (account opened within 90 days).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the sumatriptan prescription on file at home delivery: 30 tablets per fill for 90 days, written 2026-09-29.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The prescription is the baseline of the requested quantity and the evidence for the direction-change allowance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm that no home delivery shipment of sumatriptan exists in the last six months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Excludes the eligibility-fraction tier of the refill-cycle divisor (it needs at least 3 shipments) for a reader who misses the automatic refill enrollment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the retail benefit (Northbridge National Network, active) and its reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The paid retail claims and paper claims below are filed under it; it confirms the retail fills belong to the member's current benefit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the paid retail fills: sumatriptan 9 tablets every 30 days (latest 2026-09-21), Nurtec ODT fills (2026-07-02, 2026-08-13, 2026-09-12) and oxycodone-acetaminophen fills (2026-07-03, 2026-08-02).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence for the move-from-retail carryover and direction change (latest sumatriptan fill), the monthly fills at the limit for the multiple, the opioid days for the concurrent-opioid method and the Nurtec ODT fills for the preventive allowance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the sumatriptan paper claims: denied 2026-03-14 and 2026-09-03 because a coverage review was required.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Evidence for the cash-purchase units (only the 2026-09-03 denial falls within the last 6 months).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Hand the member-filed coverage review request to the caller so she can file the first-time quantity limit exception request in her own name.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The member files a first-time sumatriptan quantity limit exception request asking for 17.342 tablets per rolling 30 days; a new undecided case opens.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: review_ext_member_request_quantity uniquely produces requested_quantity_per_30; the open request is the state the approval waits on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Id: 628dc5e2-e38a-47ca-9f26-a5b6bb7229f1. Basis: returned by find_customers for member ID NBX273451906 (the caller's stated member ID). Uniqueness: the lookup narrows to exactly one profile.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.review_program_id: Id: f2676c33-0635-441d-8c57-a9679f481473. Basis: find_review_programs returns the member's single active Northbridge Clinical Standard program. Uniqueness: no other program row exists for the member.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.drug_name: Enum value sumatriptan. Basis: the caller asks for more sumatriptan; the policy names the drug as 'the drug of the member's most recent quantity limit exception case event', which is the 2026-09-30 sumatriptan information receipt. Uniqueness: Nurtec ODT has an authorization in force and is not what she asks about; every other drug is unrelated.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.drug_strength: Verbatim '100 mg tablet'. Basis: the caller reads the strength line of her label, '100 mg tablet' (user_scenario), and the home delivery prescription carries drug_strength '100 mg tablet'. Uniqueness: copied character for character.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.review_type: Enum quantity_limit_exception. Basis: tool docstring 'quantity_limit_exception when the request asks to cover more of the drug per rolling 30 days than its quantity limit allows'. Uniqueness: sumatriptan needs no prior authorization (not in the Standard package's pa_required_drugs) and has no step protocol there, so prior_authorization and step_therapy_exception do not apply.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prescriber_npi: Fixed-format 1247058369. Basis: the prescriber NPI on the home delivery prescription and on every sumatriptan claim and case. Uniqueness: the 2026-09-29 prescription the request concerns names only this prescriber.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.requested_quantity_per_30: Calculated 17.342. Prescription 30 tablets / 90 days; refill-cycle divisor = automatic refill enrolled and a supply over 34 days -> 90 - 14 lead days (Home Delivery Standard) = 76, giving 30 x 30 / 76 = 11.842105; move-from-retail carryover = account opened 2026-08-25 (42 days, within 90) and latest retail fill 2026-09-21 (15 days old, at least 7, supply not run out) -> 9 x (30 - 15) / 30 = 4.5; direction change = prescription written after that fill and directing 10.0 per 30 days against the fill's 9.0 (more, but less than 1.5 times) -> 1 unit; sum 17.342105 rounded to 3 decimals = 17.342; member-request ceiling = 9 x the whole package maximum 2.0 (a sumatriptan quantity limit authorization took effect 2025-01-14, within 24 months) = 18; the smaller is 17.342.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the quantity limit exception approval so the open request can be decided.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the approval; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Approve the member's open sumatriptan request at 17 tablets per rolling 30 days and put the quantity limit authorization in force from 2026-10-06 through 2027-10-05.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: review_ext_exception_approved_quantity uniquely produces approved_quantity_per_30 on the world after the request was filed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Id: 628dc5e2-e38a-47ca-9f26-a5b6bb7229f1. Basis: find_customers return. Uniqueness: single profile.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.review_program_id: Id: f2676c33-0635-441d-8c57-a9679f481473. Basis: find_review_programs return. Uniqueness: single program.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_case_id: Id: rvc_e14ec26463a8. Basis: the case_id in the receipt the caller read back after filing (the only undecided first-time sumatriptan quantity limit request). Uniqueness: the September case is already denied and a case takes exactly one decision.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.drug_name: Enum sumatriptan. Basis: the drug of the case being approved. Uniqueness: the case concerns only sumatriptan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.approved_quantity_per_30: Calculated 17. Requested 17.342 on the undecided request; multiple = diagnosis G43.009 (not chronic) with fills reaching 9 in each of the last three months (2026-09-21, 2026-08-22, 2026-07-23) -> seven eighths of the package maximum, 1.75, 9 x 1.75 = 15.75; concurrent opioid = 5 days supply within three months (the 2026-07-03 fill is outside) -> x 0.9 = 14.175; preventive allowance = Nurtec ODT authorization effective 2026-03-02 with 2 fills within three months (2026-07-02 is outside) -> 1; lapsed approval = sumatriptan authorization ended 2026-01-13 (within 12 months, not 6) -> 1; cash purchases = one paper claim denied 2026-09-03 for a required coverage review within 6 months (the 2026-03-14 denial is outside) -> 1; ceiling int(17.175) = 17; approved = smaller of 17.342 and 17 = 17.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.effective_date: Fixed-format 2026-10-06. Basis: rule 'the authorization it puts in force takes effect on the decision date' and base review_authorization_period 'The effective date is the decision date' (retro_effective_days is 0 at Northbridge Clinical Standard). Uniqueness: the decision is made on the call, frozen at 2026-10-06.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.expiration_date: Fixed-format 2027-10-05. Basis: base review_authorization_period 'a quantity limit exception runs ql_approval_months' (12 at Northbridge Clinical Standard) and 'The expiration date is the day before the same day-of-month that many months later'. Uniqueness: 12 months after 2026-10-06 is 2027-10-06; the day before is 2027-10-05.

factor_trace: refill_cycle_divisor (method, cross-difficulty mail): mail_accounts.5560b619-cb4c-42c1-b767-09f95cde08c5 auto_refill_enrolled=true on Northbridge Home Delivery Standard (auto_refill_lead_days 14) and the prescription mail_prescriptions.284b48da-4295-413d-8c8d-3c8b4d67e5cc is a 90-day supply (over 34) -> tier 1, divisor 90 - 14 = 76, giving 30 x 30 / 76 = 11.842105; baseline (divisor = days supply 90) gives 10.0 and result 15.5.

retail_carryover_on_move (method, cross-difficulty retail): account opened 2026-08-25 (42 days before 2026-10-06, within 90) and the latest paid sumatriptan fill retail_claims.48206a1e-c1c8-4a17-abc3-e9ad0f3497e8 on 2026-09-21 is 15 days old (at least 7) with 30 days supply -> tier 1, unused part 9 x (30 - 15) / 30 = 4.5; baseline adds nothing and gives 12.842.

direction_change_allowance (parameter): prescription written 2026-09-29, after the 2026-09-21 fill, directs 30 x 30 / 90 = 10.0 per 30 days against the fill's 9 x 30 / 30 = 9.0 (ratio 1.11, above 1 but below 1.5) -> tier 2, 1 unit; baseline 0 gives 16.342.

member_request_ceiling_multiple (parameter): review_authorizations.7b4fd2b9-7210-4b18-bfab-149cca1fea16 (sumatriptan quantity limit, effective 2025-01-14) took effect within 24 months -> tier 1, P('ql_exception_max_multiple') = 2.0, ceiling 9 x 2.0 = 18 (not binding); baseline 1.5 gives a binding ceiling of 13.5.

plain bindings: drug = sumatriptan (latest quantity limit case event, the 2026-09-30 information receipt); limit = 9; basis = prescription 30 per fill / 90 days; asked = 11.842105 + 4.5 + 1 = 17.342105 -> 17.342; result = MN(17.342, 18) = 17.342.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: enrolled in automatic home delivery refills and the prescription is written for more than a 34-day supply
account opened within the last 90 days and the latest paid retail fill dispensed at least 7 days before with supply remaining
prescription written after the latest fill directing more than that fill but less than 1.5 times it
